quizQuestions.prompt: What famous chapter of Hebrews is often called the "Hall of Faith," listing Old Testament heroes?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hebrews 11 recounts the faith of Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and many others.

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Hebrews 11:1 define faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."

options.text: The substance of things hoped for, evidence of things not seen
Only what can be proven scientifically
A feeling that fades with time

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 4:12 compare the word of God to, describing it as sharp and powerful?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 12:1 call believers to run, surrounded by a "cloud of witnesses"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Let us run with patience the race that is set before us."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 13:8 say about Jesus Christ, describing His unchanging nature?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 4:15 say about Jesus as high priest, regarding our weaknesses?
quizQuestions.explanation: He was "touched with the feeling of our infirmities... yet without sin."

options.text: He was touched with the feeling of our infirmities
He was unaware of human struggles
He refused to relate to human weakness
He was untouched by any human experience

quizQuestions.prompt: Hebrews uniquely argues that Jesus is superior to which Old Testament figures and systems?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hebrews argues Jesus is greater than the angels, Moses, and the Levitical priesthood and its sacrifices.

options.text: Angels, Moses, and the Levitical priesthood

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 9:22 say is necessary for the remission (forgiveness) of sins?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Without shedding of blood is no remission."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 10:25 encourage believers not to forsake?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hebrews 13:2 say might happen when believers entertain strangers?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares."

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Hebrews 1:1-2, how has God ultimately spoken to humanity, after speaking through the prophets?
quizQuestions.explanation: God has now spoken through His Son.

options.text: Through a new set of angels

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Hebrews 12:2 give Jesus, in relation to believers' faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith."

options.text: The author and finisher of our faith
Only a good example, nothing more

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notable about the authorship of Hebrews, unlike Paul's other letters?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hebrews never names its author, and its authorship has been debated since the early church.

options.text: The author is never named and remains debated
It clearly names Paul as the author
It clearly names Peter as the author
It is signed by all twelve apostles

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Hebrews 11, what did Noah do "by faith" when warned of things not yet seen?
quizQuestions.explanation: By faith, Noah prepared an ark for the saving of his household.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 1:2-4 say to count trials as, since they produce patience?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 1:22 urge believers to be, not just hearers of the word?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 2:17 say about faith that has no accompanying works?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone."

options.text: It is more valuable than active faith

quizQuestions.prompt: What small but powerful body part does James 3 compare to a spark that can set a whole forest ablaze?
quizQuestions.explanation: James compares the tongue to a small fire capable of great destruction.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 4:7 say will happen if believers resist the devil?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Resist the devil, and he will flee from you."

options.text: He will attack twice as hard

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 5:16 say "availeth much," when offered by a righteous person?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 1:5 say to do if someone lacks wisdom?
quizQuestions.explanation: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally."

options.text: Ask no one and figure it out alone

quizQuestions.prompt: What practice does James 5:14-15 describe for praying over someone who is sick?
quizQuestions.explanation: Anointing the sick person with oil and praying the prayer of faith over them.

options.text: Anointing them with oil and praying over them

quizQuestions.prompt: Which New Testament James, who led the Jerusalem church and presided over its council in Acts 15, is traditionally credited as the author of the book of James?
quizQuestions.explanation: James, the brother of Jesus, is traditionally credited as the author.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does James 4:14 compare human life to, describing its brief nature?
quizQuestions.explanation: "It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away."

quizQuestions.prompt: How does James 1:27 define "pure religion and undefiled before God"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Visiting orphans and widows in their affliction, and keeping oneself unspotted from the world.

options.text: Caring for orphans and widows, staying unspotted from the world
Accumulating wealth for the poor to see

quizQuestions.prompt: According to James 2:26, what is faith without works compared to?
quizQuestions.explanation: "As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 5:8 compare "your adversary the devil" to, walking about seeking whom he may devour?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour."

quizQuestions.prompt: What titles does 1 Peter 2:9 give believers, describing their identity in Christ?
quizQuestions.explanation: "A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation."

options.text: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 4:8 say charity (love) does, regarding a multitude of sins?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Charity shall cover the multitude of sins."

options.text: It covers a multitude of sins
It has no effect on sin

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 5:7 instruct believers to cast upon God, since He cares for them?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 3:15 say believers should always be ready to give?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you."

options.text: A reason for the hope within them
A portion of their wealth only

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was 1 Peter primarily written to, according to its opening address in 1:1?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter wrote to Christians dispersed across Asia Minor, facing suffering as exiles.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 2:24 say about how believers were healed, quoting Isaiah's suffering servant?
quizQuestions.explanation: "By whose stripes ye were healed," referring to Christ bearing our sins on the tree.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 1:6-7 compare trials of faith to, something tested and refined?
quizQuestions.explanation: Faith tried is compared to gold refined by fire, proven more precious.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Peter 2:21 say Christ left believers, by His suffering?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps."

quizQuestions.prompt: What circumstance were the believers Peter wrote to primarily facing, which the letter offers hope through?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter wrote to encourage Christians facing suffering and persecution.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Peter 1:20-21 say about how Scripture came to be written?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost," not by private interpretation.

options.text: Holy men spoke as moved by the Holy Ghost
Each writer invented their own private ideas
It was written entirely by angels
It was translated from an unknown source

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Peter 3:9 say about the Lord's patience regarding His promise to return?
quizQuestions.explanation: He is longsuffering, "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance."

options.text: He is patient, not wanting any to perish
He is eager to destroy the earth quickly
He has given up on humanity

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does 2 Peter 3:8 make about time, from God's perspective?
quizQuestions.explanation: "One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day."

options.text: A day is like a thousand years to Him
Time means nothing at all to God
A thousand years passes in a moment for everyone
God experiences time exactly as humans do

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does 2 Peter 3:10 use to describe how the day of the Lord will come?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night."

options.text: As a thief in the night
Only to a chosen few in advance

quizQuestions.prompt: What list of virtues does 2 Peter 1:5-7 urge believers to add to their faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: Virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity.

options.text: Virtue, knowledge, patience, godliness, and charity

quizQuestions.prompt: What group does 2 Peter 2 warn extensively against, troubling the early church with dangerous teaching?
quizQuestions.explanation: 2 Peter warns against false teachers and false prophets.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Peter say about Paul's letters in 2 Peter 3:15-16, acknowledging some parts were difficult?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter calls Paul's letters Scripture, alongside "the other scriptures," while noting some things are "hard to be understood."

options.text: He called them Scripture, though hard to understand in places
He said they contradicted his own teaching
He refused to mention them at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Peter insist the apostles were, not followers of "cunningly devised fables," in 2 Peter 1:16?
quizQuestions.explanation: He insists they were "eyewitnesses of his majesty," likely referring to the Transfiguration.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 1:9 promise happens when believers confess their sins?
quizQuestions.explanation: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins."

options.text: God forgives them, being faithful and just

quizQuestions.prompt: What simple, famous declaration does 1 John 4:8 make about God's nature?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God is love."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 4:18 say perfect love does, regarding fear?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Perfect love casteth out fear."

options.text: It has no effect on fear

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 1:5 declare about God, that in Him is no darkness at all?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God is light, and in him is no darkness at all."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 3:1 marvel at, regarding believers being called "sons of God"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God."

options.text: The Father's great love in calling us His children
The distance between God and man
The impossibility of being called God's children

quizQuestions.prompt: What purpose does John give for writing his first letter, in 1 John 5:13?
quizQuestions.explanation: So that believers "may know that ye have eternal life."

options.text: So readers would know they have eternal life
To record a history of Rome

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 4:19 say is the reason believers love God?
quizQuestions.explanation: "We love him, because he first loved us."

options.text: Because it is required by law

quizQuestions.prompt: What early heresy about Jesus' physical nature does 1 John call "the spirit of antichrist"?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 John warns against an early denial of Christ's true humanity, calling it the spirit of antichrist.

options.text: Denying Jesus came in the flesh

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 4:1 instruct believers to do with "every spirit," rather than believe blindly?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God."

options.text: Test them to see if they are of God

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 John 2:15 instruct believers not to love?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world."

options.text: The world and the things in it

quizQuestions.prompt: To whom is 2 John addressed, an unusual address among New Testament letters?
quizQuestions.explanation: It is addressed to "the elect lady and her children," possibly a woman or a symbolic reference to a church.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 John 1:6 say love means, in practical terms?
quizQuestions.explanation: "This is love, that we walk after his commandments."

quizQuestions.prompt: What warning does 2 John give about receiving false teachers into one's house?
quizQuestions.explanation: Believers are warned not to receive or even greet them, to avoid sharing in their evil deeds.

options.text: Not to receive or greet them
To argue with them at length

quizQuestions.prompt: How many chapters does the short letter of 2 John contain?
quizQuestions.explanation: 2 John has just one chapter.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does John rejoice about at the start of 2 John, regarding some of the lady's children?
quizQuestions.explanation: He rejoices to find some of her children "walking in truth."

quizQuestions.prompt: To whom is 3 John addressed personally, praised for his hospitality and faithfulness?
quizQuestions.explanation: 3 John is addressed to Gaius.

quizQuestions.prompt: What wish does John express for Gaius as the letter of 3 John opens?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth."

options.text: That he would prosper and be in health as his soul prospers
That he would give up all his possessions
That he would leave his home
That he would face great hardship

quizQuestions.prompt: Who does John rebuke in 3 John for loving to have preeminence and refusing to welcome traveling teachers?
quizQuestions.explanation: John rebukes Diotrephes for his prideful, unwelcoming behavior.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is commended with a good report by everyone, including "of the truth itself," near the end of 3 John?
quizQuestions.explanation: Demetrius is given a good report by all, and by the truth itself.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notable about the length of 3 John, like 2 John, compared to most New Testament books?
quizQuestions.explanation: 3 John is one of the shortest books in the Bible, just one chapter.

options.text: It is one of the shortest books, just one chapter
It is one of the longest letters Paul wrote
It is longer than the Gospels

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Jude 1:3 urge believers to earnestly do for the faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."

quizQuestions.prompt: What unusual event does Jude 1:9 reference, involving the archangel Michael disputing with the devil?
quizQuestions.explanation: Michael disputed with the devil about the body of Moses.

options.text: A dispute over the body of Moses
A battle over the Ark of the Covenant
A dispute over the Temple's gold

quizQuestions.prompt: Jude's letter shares significant content and warnings with which other short New Testament book?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jude closely parallels 2 Peter, both warning against false teachers.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Jude's closing doxology say about God's power over believers, right before praising Him as "the only wise God our Saviour"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless."

options.text: "Unto him that is able to keep you from falling"
"The LORD bless thee and keep thee"

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Jude describe his relationship to Jesus, though tradition identifies him as Jesus' half-brother?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jude humbly calls himself only "the servant of Jesus Christ," not claiming his family relationship.

quizQuestions.prompt: Jude quotes a prophecy from which figure, not included in most Old Testament canons, about the Lord coming with ten thousand of His saints?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jude quotes a prophecy attributed to Enoch.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did John see standing in the midst of seven golden candlesticks in his opening vision?
quizQuestions.explanation: John saw "one like unto the Son of man" among the candlesticks.

options.text: One like unto the Son of man

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Jesus give Himself in Revelation 1:8, describing His eternal nature?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord."

quizQuestions.prompt: How many churches in Asia does John address directly with letters in Revelation 2-3?
quizQuestions.explanation: John addresses seven churches in Asia Minor.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Revelation 4-5, who alone is found worthy to open the sealed scroll before God's throne?
quizQuestions.explanation: A Lamb, representing Christ, is the only one worthy to open the scroll.

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision in Revelation 6 involves riders on white, red, black, and pale horses?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, riding white, red, black, and pale horses.

quizQuestions.prompt: What symbolic vision of cosmic conflict appears in Revelation chapter 12?
quizQuestions.explanation: Revelation 12 describes this symbolic vision of conflict between good and evil.

options.text: A woman clothed with the sun and a great red dragon
A city built entirely of gold

quizQuestions.prompt: What well-known number is associated with the beast rising out of the sea in Revelation 13?
quizQuestions.explanation: The number of the beast is given as 666.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Revelation 19, what title is written on the rider of the white horse, described as "Faithful and True"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS."

options.text: "KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does an angel do to Satan for a thousand years in Revelation 20?
quizQuestions.explanation: An angel binds Satan for a thousand years, often called the Millennium.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does John see at the start of Revelation 21, once everything from the old creation has passed away?
quizQuestions.explanation: "A new heaven and a new earth."

options.text: A new heaven and a new earth
A return to the original Eden only

quizQuestions.prompt: How is the New Jerusalem described coming down from God in Revelation 21:2?
quizQuestions.explanation: "As a bride adorned for her husband."

options.text: As a bride adorned for her husband

quizQuestions.prompt: What comforting promise does Revelation 21:4 give about tears and death in the new creation?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death."

options.text: God will wipe away all tears, and death will end
Tears and death will simply be ignored
Only the righteous will stop crying
Death will continue, but tears will end

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Jesus repeat about Himself in Revelation 22:13, near the very end of the Bible?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last."

options.text: "Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"

quizQuestions.prompt: What book is opened at the final judgment scene in Revelation 20, alongside other books, determining each person's fate?
quizQuestions.explanation: The book of life is opened, along with other books recording deeds.

options.text: The Book of the Law only

quizQuestions.prompt: What warning does Revelation end with, about not adding to or taking away from something?
quizQuestions.explanation: A solemn warning about adding to or taking away from "the words of the prophecy of this book."

options.text: The words of the prophecy of this book
The laws of the Roman Empire

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Revelation describe itself as being, given to reveal things that must shortly come to pass?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The Revelation of Jesus Christ."
